title: What do we see in a rectangle whose diagonal cuts a corner equally?
description: A rectangle is built so that its diagonal divides the opposite angles into forty five degrees and forty five degrees, and then the sides are measured. All four sides turn out to be equal, so the rectangle is a square.
teaching_notes: One idea: the same order of drawing gives the rectangle, and two equal angles at a corner force the sides to be equal. Watch for students who stop after the drawing and do not measure the sides.

video_script.why: A learner builds the rectangle with a diagonal that cuts the corner equally, measures its sides, and sees that all four are equal.
video_script.substitution: the rectangle ABCD with the diagonal AC making forty five degrees with the side AB
video_script.anchor: a rough rectangle ABCD with the diagonal AC, the angles at A marked 45 degrees and 45 degrees
video_script.payoff_line: The rectangle is ready. All four sides are equal, so it is a square.

final_answer.value: rectangle ABCD built with 45 degrees at A next to AB and 45 degrees next to AD; all the sides are equal, so it is a square
final_answer.spoken: the rectangle is built and all its sides are equal, so it is a square

hold_back: Answer: all the sides are equal
maths_rules: each corner of a rectangle is 90 degrees
the other angle at A is 90 - 45 = 45 degrees
AB = BC = CD = DA when measured
a rectangle with all four sides equal is a square
